portal_hypertension.abstract: Portopulmonary hypertension (PoPH) is a complex and underrecognized form of pulmonary arterial hypertension arising in the setting of portal hypertension, in which outcomes are driven by the interplay between pulmonary vascular disease and liver dysfunction. Despite advances in hemodynamic definitions and targeted therapies, PoPH remains associated with significant morbidity and mortality, largely due to delayed diagnosis, challenges in risk stratification, and the absence of disease-specific management strategies. portal_hypertension.abstract: Portal hypertension has a limited pharmacological armamentarium despite decades of preclinical therapeutic research. We mapped the experimental architecture of this literature, independently of reported treatment efficacy. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Two independent title-and-abstract screening procedures identified 833 records retained by at least one screen; 540 formed a concordant core retained by both. Records were classified using a prespecified taxonomy of therapeutic strategy, intervention modality, animal model, species, sex, treatment schedule and reporting features. portal_hypertension.abstract: Patients suffering from acute esophagogastric variceal bleeding (AEGVB) frequently face unfavorable prognoses. Although endoscopy is the preferred intervention for AEGVB, the optimal timing for its administration to enhance patient outcomes remains a subject of ongoing debate. This study encompassed patients with cirrhosis who presented with AEGVB and received endoscopic treatment at three major tertiary hospitals in Shandong Province, China, from January 2017 to July 2024. Participants were stratified based on the time interval from hospital admission to endoscopic intervention (<12 hours vs. ≥12 hours; <24 hours vs. ≥24 hours; <48 hours vs. ≥48 hours; <72 hours vs. ≥72 hours). portal_hypertension.abstract: While an association between trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) and development of portal hypertension has been suggested, clinical studies on the incidence and risk factors remain limited. HER2-positive breast cancer patients treated with T-DM1 as adjuvant or palliative therapy were retrospectively enrolled. The composite endpoint of portal hypertension and sinusoidal liver injury was defined as development of splenomegaly and at least one among gastroesophageal varices, spontaneous portosystemic shunt, or portal hypertensive ascites; or biopsy-confirmed sinusoidal obstruction syndrome.
